criteria.text: `GET /api/people/:id/attention?days=30` (#211, already merged — not re-tested here) returns `200` with `{ days: 30, series: [] }`, never a non-2xx status, for a person with no `wikipedia` alias. This spec's own tests stub the response via `routeFetch` and never hit a real database.

`peakDay` on a series with a single maximum returns that day; on a tie between two or more days sharing the maximum value, returns the earliest (oldest) of the tied days; on an all-zero series, returns `null`.

The lag sentence renders "a imprensa veio N dias antes" when the mentions peak precedes the views peak by N days (N ≥ 1), "o público buscou N dias antes" when the views peak precedes the mentions peak by N days, "os dois picos caíram no mesmo dia" when both peaks fall on the same day, and no sentence (a note instead) when either series has no peak (all-zero).

The mentions row's per-day sizes and the views row's per-day sizes are computed from independent maxima: a fixture where mentions are uniformly small (max 3) and views are uniformly large (max 50000) does not make every mentions bar render at floor size relative to a views-scaled ramp — each row's own largest day renders at that row's own ceiling size.
`attentionParams(...)` always sends `days=30` regardless of any other input, matching `weekParams`'s fixed-`days=7` precedent.
The mentions-series request omits `term` (or sends `term=''`), sends `kind` as the full atlas kind set, and covers whatever `source` the figure's own control selects — never filtered to one term.

`src/ui/figures/attention.ts` exports exactly `mount`, does not touch `document` at import time, and is never imported by (and never imports) `atlas.ts`, `testimony.ts`, `compare.ts`, `rising.ts`, `week.ts` or `lenses.ts`. Checkable by adding a `figures/attention.ts` entry to `test/invariants.test.ts`'s existing per-module allowed-imports map (the `figures/lenses.ts` entry there, `test/invariants.test.ts:146`, is the exact precedent) — this is one new map entry, not a new kind of assertion.

Clicking a day column opens `#docsDialog` with `owner: 'attention'`, one side, `day` set to that column's UTC date string, `term: ''`, and `kind` the atlas's full kind set; clicking the same day again (or a background click, or Escape) releases it.

A person with an empty `/attention` response still renders the figure (present in the DOM, in `FIGURES`), with the views row at floor size, a "sem dado de pageviews para esta pessoa" note, and no lag sentence; the mentions row renders normally from `/timeline`.

`paintAttentionLoading` returns a ghost with the same two-row/axis shape `paintAttention` draws with data — matching every other figure's ghost-shape convention (`test/render.test.ts`'s existing per-painter pattern is the template for two new tests here, one per state).

`public/como-ler.html` contains an element with `id="atencao"` whose surrounding text states, as facts (loosely matched, not pinned to one exact sentence): that Wikipedia pageviews measure curiosity rather than opinion, and that the two series are drawn on two independently-scaled rows rather than compared as one number against another. This follows the existing precedent for testing this page's own content (`test/leitura-ui-acceptance.test.ts`'s `<div id="avaliacao">...` extraction-then-fact-match, not `test/docs.ts`'s `docsText` — `como-ler.html` is UI copy, not part of `docPages`, which is `README.md` plus `docs/*.md` only).

`public/atlas.html`'s new `#attention` section carries a `.figure-key` and a "Como ler" link targeting `como-ler.html#atencao`. This extends `test/leitura-ui-acceptance.test.ts`'s existing "the page is a sequence of graphs" test, which already hardcodes the figure id list, the eyebrow-per-figure regexes, the figure count, and the total `.pick` count — those literal arrays/numbers (`['workspace', 'testimony', 'compare', 'rising', 'week', 'lenses']` → add `'attention'`; figure-sub count 6 → 7; add a `Gráfico 7` assertion; the shared `.pick` total → +2 for attention's own person/source sentence) must be edited by hand to include the seventh figure; this is not a fact this issue asserts fresh.
No `font-size: …px` literal is introduced by the new CSS rules (`test/leitura-ui-acceptance.test.ts`'s whole-stylesheet scan already covers this; no new test needed).
`pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass with the new module, types and CSS in place; `pnpm build` is re-run and `public/bundle.js` committed (`test/bundle-freshness.test.ts`).
